title: Mizzen diagnostics
description: The `mizzen check --format json` envelope: version 1 and the build's findings in stable order. A position is an inclusive source span in Unicode code points; a fix is a replacement a tool can apply without reading prose.

diagnostics.description: Findings sorted by file, line, column, then id; findings without a position come last.

column.description: 1-based column in the source file, counting Unicode code points; a tab is one column.

diagnostic.description: One finding with the place and the repair that are known for it.

fix.description: A safe, mechanical repair on one source span, when there is one.

help.description: How to fix the problem, when the repair is known but is not mechanical.

id.description: The stable check ID, such as `config.unknown-key`; an ID is never reused for another meaning.

message.description: What is wrong, in one sentence.

pos.description: Where in the source the problem is, when it has a place.

severity.description: An error fails the build; a warning is reported; info is for the reader only.

diagnosticFix.description: Replace the characters of one source span with `text`; an empty `text` deletes the span.

column.description: Column where the replaced span starts.

description.description: A short phrase for people, such as `Add a trailing slash`.

endColumn.description: Column of the replaced span's last character (inclusive).

endLine.description: Line where the replaced span ends; the same as `line` for a one-line span.

line.description: Line where the replaced span starts.

text.description: What replaces the span; the empty string deletes it.

line.description: 1-based line in the source file, front matter included.

path.description: A path relative to the repository root, with forward slashes.

sourcePos.description: A span from its first character to its last. The end is inclusive, so it names the last character, and it is never before the start; JSON Schema cannot compare the four numbers, so the engine guarantees the order.

endColumn.description: Column of the span's last character (inclusive).

endLine.description: Line where the span ends; the same as `line` for a one-line span.
